answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table (security patch must not be reverted), so memory_b1/b6 guidance doesn't apply. The symptom is write-path p99 latency during the daily settlement peak, which points to capacity pressure rather than a partner dependency failure (circuit breaker, b4) or a regional fault (failover, b2 — no evidence the degradation is regional). Read replicas (b5) offload read queries only and would not relieve write latency, so I want to verify b5 to confirm its scope before ruling it out. Adding capacity (b3) directly matches heavy write load at peak and historically absorbed surges without customer impact; I verify b3 to confirm it applied to write-path load, not just queue depth. Capacity adds are reversible and low-risk to customer writes.
